why: The substring must be contiguous and duplicate-free, so maintain a window [start, i] with no repeats: extend the right end one character at a time and, when the new character already appears inside the window, jump start past its last occurrence.
hints: If s[start..i] has no repeats and s[i+1] repeats something in it, which starts can still work?
Only starts after the previous occurrence of s[i+1]. Remember each character's last index; when that index is >= start, move start to last + 1.
One pass with a dict char -> last index and a running best of i - start + 1. O(n) time, O(alphabet) space.
pitfalls: Only move start forward: a last occurrence before start is outside the window and must be ignored.
Characters include digits, symbols and spaces, not just lowercase letters; a dict handles all of them.
A string of one repeated character has answer 1, not 0.
statement:
Given a string s, return the length of the longest contiguous substring in which no character appears twice. s may contain English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.

Worked example: s = "abcabcbb"

  • Window grows to "abc" (length 3).
  • Next a repeats the a at index 0, so the window starts at index 1: "bca".
  • Continuing the same way the window becomes "cab", "abc", then "cb" and "b"; it never exceeds 3.

Answer: 3. For "bbbbb" every valid window is a single b, so the answer is 1.
